nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
إِذا is in the position of the accusative because it is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), and what governs it is وقعت, because it resembles the conditional particles, and [with those] only what comes after them governs them. Sībawayh reported that some Arabs use it to put [the verb] in the jussive. He said: its resemblance to the conditional particles is firm and strong, because it turns the past into the future and requires an apodosis (jawāb), except that it is not used to make a [jussive] conditional except in poetry. As for how it differs from the conditional particles: what comes after it is something definite; you say "I will come to you when the unripe dates turn red," and «أن» [Translator's note: presumably the conditional «إن»] is not permissible here. The tāʾ of «وقعت» was given kasra because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, since it is a particle and its rule is to be vowelless.

Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: al-Wāqiʿa (the Event), al-Ṭāmma (the Overwhelming Calamity), al-Ṣākhkha (the Deafening Blast) and the like are among the names of the Resurrection; Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has made it great and warned His servants of it. Someone else said: it is the Shout, which is the first blowing [of the Trumpet].

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: [كاذبة is] the noun of ليس. Most grammarians hold that كاذبة was given the feminine because it has the meaning of "lying" (الكذب) [i.e. a maṣdar], i.e. there is no lie in its occurring. al-Farrāʾ said: like عاقبة and عافية.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
خافِضَةٌ رافِعَةٌ (3): by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject); the implied form is "the Event is abasing, exalting." al-Yazīdī read خافِضَةٌ رافِعَةٌ in the accusative [i.e. خافضةً رافعةً]. This reading is anomalous (shādhdh) and abandoned, from more than one angle. Among them: the multitude [of readers], by whom the proof is established, read against it. Among them: the meaning requires the nominative, according to the people of tafsīr and the meticulous scholars among the people of Arabic.

As for the people of tafsīr, Ibn ʿAbbās said: it abased some people and exalted others. On this view only the nominative is permissible, because the meaning is: it abased into the Fire people who were mighty in the world and exalted into the Garden people who were lowly in the world. If it were put in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the ḥāl would entail that the matter could possibly be otherwise, just as when you say "Zayd came hurrying," it would have been possible for him to come in a state other than this one. ʿIkrima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: خافِضَةٌ رافِعَةٌ: it lowered [its voice] and made the nearest hear, and raised [it] and made the farthest hear, so people became equal.

Abū Jaʿfar said: As for the people of Arabic, a group of them discussed the accusative. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: it is not permissible. al-Farrāʾ said: it is permissible, meaning "when the Event befalls, it befalls abasing, exalting," implying [a second] وقعت; but in the view of other grammarians this is far-fetched and ugly. If you said "when I come to you as a visitor" (إذا جئتك زائرا), meaning "when I come to you, I come to you as a visitor," this implying would not be permissible, because its meaning would not be recognised, and the hearer might imagine that something of the speech remained. Abū Isḥāq permitted the accusative on the basis that «وقعت» governs the ḥāl; we have explained its unsoundness. Moreover, everyone who permitted it construes it as anomalous, and this suffices for abandoning it.

nahhas-irab:4-5.t: إِذا is in the position of the accusative. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is "when the Event befalls at this time." رَجًّا is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and likewise وَبُسَّتِ الْجِبالُ بَسًّا (5).

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: هَباءً: the khabar (predicate) of كان. مُنْبَثًّا: [part] of its naʿt (adjective). The soundest thing said about its meaning is what is related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him; he said: الهباء المنبثّ is the dust raised by the riding animals. From Ibn ʿAbbās: it is dust; and from him: it is the sparks that fly from fire.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: From Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: three classes. Abū Isḥāq said: classes that go together with one another are called أزواج, the singular being زوج, just as one says "a زوج of khuffs" for one of the two khuffs.

nahhas-irab:8-9.t:
فَأَصْحابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ: nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). ما أَصْحابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ: a mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate), in the position of the khabar of the first. It was said: the implied form is "what are they?"; therefore it is fit to be the khabar of the first, since a reference to it returns to it. Likewise الْقارِعَةُ مَا الْقارِعَةُ [al-Qāriʿa: 1, 2]: the noun is stated overtly by way of magnification and intensification. This is a good view, because repeating the noun carries the sense of magnification; and likewise فَأَصْحابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ ما أَصْحابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ (8).

It was said: they were only called "the Companions of the Right" because they were given their books in their right hands. It was also said: because they are taken towards the right, and this is a sign on the Day of Resurrection of one who is saved. It was also said: the Garden is on people's right on the Day of Resurrection. On this basis [is] وَأَصْحابُ الْمَشْئَمَةِ ما أَصْحابُ الْمَشْئَمَةِ (9), because the left hand is called الشّومى.

nahhas-irab:10-11.t:
Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn said: the forerunners (al-sābiqūn) are those who prayed towards both qiblas. Abū Isḥāq holds that there are two analyses of it in Arabic. One of them is that the first السابقون is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) and the second is [part] of its description, and the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ is أُولئِكَ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ (11). He also permits that the first السابقون be nominative as mubtadaʾ and the [second] السابقون be its khabar, its implied form being: "and those foremost in obedience to Allah are those foremost to the mercy of Allah"; he said: أولئك المقربون is a description.

Abū Jaʿfar said: His saying that أولئك is a description is an error in my view, because what has the alif and lām cannot be described with a vague noun (mubham, i.e. demonstrative). According to Sībawayh, مررت بالرجل ذلك and مررت بالرجل هذا are not permissible as naʿt (adjective). The reason for this is that the vague noun is more definite than what has the alif and lām, and according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh a thing is only described by what is below it in definiteness. Rather, أولئك المقربون is a badal (substitute) or a khabar after a khabar.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: [It is] part of the ṣila (relative clause) of المقرّبين, or another khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is "they are a multitude from the earlier ones."

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: عَلى سُرُرٍ: Some Arabs say سرر [i.e. surar, with fatḥa] because of the heaviness of the ḍamma and the repetition of the letter, and in the rāʾ there is also repetition [i.e. trilling]. مَوْضُونَةٍ: a naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: Abū Isḥāq said: they are both accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: al-Farrāʾ mentioned that its meaning is "of one age, not changing," as though it were derived from birth (al-wilāda), except that one says: وليد بين الولادة ("a child of evident childhood") with fatḥa on the wāw.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: بِأَكْوابٍ: the plural of paucity sufficed in place of [the plural of] multitude. وَأَبارِيقَ: it is not fully declined because it is a plural with no counterpart among singulars. وَكَأْسٍ: a singular that conveys the plural. It is related from Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa from Ibn ʿAbbās on وَكَأْسٍ مِنْ مَعِينٍ; he said: wine. al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: every كأس in the Qur'an is wine. Qatāda said: من معين, i.e. of wine that is seen with the eyes [flowing].

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: لا يُصَدَّعُونَ عَنْها وَلا يُنْزِفُونَ (19) لا يُصَدَّعُونَ عَنْها وَلا يُنْزِفُونَ: So He negated of the wine the harms that attend it, of intoxication and headache. It was also said: «يصدّعون عنها» means they are dispersed from it out of aversion.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: i.e. which they choose; the hāʾ [of the resumptive pronoun] was dropped because of the length of the noun [i.e. the relative clause].

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: Among the people of tafsīr there are those who say: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, creates for them meat according to what they desire, roasted or cooked, of the kind of fowl; and among them there are those who say: rather, it is the meat of birds in reality. With this the ḥadīth came from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd from the Prophet ﷺ; he said: "It is no more than that you desire a bird in the Garden while it is flying, and it falls before you roasted."

nahhas-irab:22-23.t:
وَحُورٌ عِينٌ (22) is the reading of Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, Shayba and Nāfiʿ. al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read وَحُورٌ عِينٌ in the genitive [i.e. وحورٍ عينٍ]. Sībawayh and al-Farrāʾ reported that in the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb it is وحورا عينا in the accusative. Sībawayh claimed that the nominative is construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is "in it are cups, ewers, a cup from a flowing spring, fruit, the meat of birds, and ḥūr," i.e. and they have wide-eyed ḥūr. And he recited: [kāmil metre] 451-
بادت وغيّر ايهنّ مع البلى ... إلّا رواكد جمرهنّ هباء
ومشجّج أمّا سوعاء قذاله ... فبدا وغيّر ساره المعزاء
(They [the abodes] have perished, and decay has altered their signs, except for the fixed hearth-stones whose embers are dust; and a battered [tent-peg], whose head-part has appeared, while the rough ground has altered the rest of it.)
So he put ومشجّج in the nominative according to the meaning, because the meaning is "in it are fixed [stones], and in it is a battered [peg]."

The nominative reading is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd, because the ḥūr are not passed around [among them]. al-Farrāʾ chose the genitive and argued that the fruit and the meat are not passed around either; only the wine is passed around. We do not know how this argument stands, since the readers have agreed on reading the genitive in His saying, Majestic and Mighty, وَفاكِهَةٍ مِمَّا يَتَخَيَّرُونَ (20) وَلَحْمِ طَيْرٍ مِمَّا يَشْتَهُونَ (21). So where does he get it that these things, which he claimed are not passed around, are not passed around? One only yields in this to a decisive proof or a report that must be accepted.

They differed over His saying, Majestic and Mighty, وَحُورٌ عِينٌ (22), as I mentioned. The genitive is permissible by construing it according to the meaning, because the meaning is "they enjoy these things and enjoy wide-eyed ḥūr"; this is permissible and frequent in Arabic, as [the poet] said: [kāmil metre] 452-
علفتها تبنا وماء باردا ... حتّى شتت همّالة عيناها
(I fed her straw and cool water, until she wintered with her eyes streaming.)
So it was construed according to the meaning. Another said: [majzūʾ al-kāmil metre] 453-
يا ليت زوجك قد غدا ... متقلّدا سيفا ورمحا
(Would that your husband had gone out in the morning girded with a sword and a spear.)
And another said: [wāfir metre] 454-
إذا ما الغانيات برزن يوما ... وزجّجن الحواجب والعيونا
(When the beautiful women come out one day and have finely drawn their eyebrows and their eyes.)
Eyes are not "drawn fine," so he construed it according to the meaning. As for «وحورا عينا», it is also construed according to the meaning, because the meaning of the first is "they are given this, and they are given ḥūr," as [the poet] said: [basīṭ metre] 455-
جئني بمثل بني بدر لقومهم ... أو مثل أسرة منظور بن سيّار أو عامر بن طفيل في مركّبه ... أو حارثا يوم نادى القوم يا حار
(Bring me the like of Banū Badr for their people, or the like of the family of Manẓūr ibn Sayyār, or ʿĀmir ibn Ṭufayl in his lineage, or Ḥārith on the day the people called out "O Ḥār!")

al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said: الحور are those whose black of the eye is intensely black [Translator's note: the printed text repeats «سواد سواد»]. This is the best of what has been said about their meaning. الحور [also means] whiteness, and from it is الحوّاريّ (fine white flour). It is related from Mujāhid that he said: they are called حور because the eye is bewildered (taḥāru) by them. al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: العين are those with large eyes. Abū Jaʿfar said: عين is the plural of عيناء, and it is on the pattern fuʿl, except that the fāʾ [first radical] was given kasra so that the yāʾ would not turn into wāw and be confused with the wāw-roots. al-Farrāʾ reported that some Arabs say حير عين by assimilation (itbāʿ).

It is related from Umm Salama; she said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell me about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: كَأَمْثالِ اللُّؤْلُؤِ الْمَكْنُونِ (23)." He said: "Like the clarity of the pearl that is in the shell, which no hands touch."

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: Abū Isḥāq said: You put جزاء in the accusative because it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. as a reward for their deeds. He said: it may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ (17) is "He rewards them with that, as a reward for their deeds."

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: اللّغو is whatever is discarded [as worthless]. It was said: its meaning is that they do not hear in it clamour, nor irritation, nor shouting. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, negated of the people of the Garden everything that befalls people in the world in their enjoyment, of irritation; and in everything of the harms that befall their food and drink; and everything of toil and fatigue that befalls them; and in the food and drink in this sūra. In one ḥadīth: "Whoever persists in reciting Sūrat al-Wāqiʿa every day will never become poor."

nahhas-irab:26-26.t:
Abū Isḥāq said: إِلَّا قِيلًا is accusative by يسمعون, i.e. they hear nothing but speech. Someone else said: it is accusative as the excepted (exception). سَلاماً سَلاماً may be a naʿt (adjective) of قيل, i.e. except speech that is free of shouting, clamour and what involves sin. It may be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). A third way is permissible: that it is accusative by قيل, the meaning of قيل being "that they say." al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ permitted the nominative in سلام, in the sense of "peace be upon you," and al-Farrāʾ recited: [ṭawīl metre] 456-
فقلنا السّلام فاتّقت من أميرها ... فما كان إلّا ومؤها بالحواجب
(We said "Peace!", but she was wary of her guardian, so there was nothing but her signalling with the eyebrows.)

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: وَأَصْحابُ الْيَمِينِ: There are three views on its meaning. Among them: they were only called the Companions of the Right because they were given their books in their right hands. Among them: they will be taken towards the right on the Day of Resurrection, and that is the mark of one who is saved. The third view is that they are those whom Allah, Majestic and Mighty, swore [lit. took an oath, yamīn] to admit into the Garden. ما أَصْحابُ الْيَمِينِ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), in the position of the khabar of the first. The view of Qatāda: the meaning is "what a thing it is, and what good things have been prepared for them!"

nahhas-irab:28-29.t: «مخضود»: The soundest thing said about it is that its thorns have been cut off. It was also said: it is created like that. The Arabs know الطّلح as a tree with many thorns. Abū Isḥāq said: it may be in the Garden with the thorns removed from it. The people of tafsīr say: الطلح is the banana. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: this may be among what the authors of [books on] rare words did not transmit; the names of plants are numerous, so much so that the people of language say: one who makes a scribal mistake in the names of plants is not blamed, because of how many they are.

nahhas-irab:30-31.t: i.e. one does not toil in drawing it.

nahhas-irab:32-33.t: وَفاكِهَةٍ كَثِيرَةٍ (32) لا مَقْطُوعَةٍ: a naʿt (adjective). It was permissible to separate the naʿt from the qualified noun by your saying لا because of its wide range of use and because it occurs as redundant (zāʾida). Qatāda said about the meaning of وَلا مَمْنُوعَةٍ: neither thorns nor distance prevent [anyone] from it.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: i.e. high; from it [comes] "a lofty (rafīʿ) building."

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: Mujāhid said: they were created from saffron. Abū Isḥāq said: a bringing into being without birth.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: A second object. Abū ʿUbayda said about the pronoun in «أنشأناهنّ» that it refers back to «وحور عين». al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: it is a pronoun to which no prior mention has been made, except that its meaning is known.

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: عُرُباً is the plural of عروب; the dialect of Tamīm and Najd is عربا [i.e. ʿurban], dropping the ḍamma because of its heaviness. أَتْراباً is the plural of ترب.

nahhas-irab:38-40.t:
The meaning is: We brought them into being for the Companions of the Right. In the ḥadīth from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, and Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah have mercy on them both, they both said: the Companions of the Right are the children of the believers.

al-Farrāʾ analysed it in the sense of "the Companions of the Right have a multitude from the earlier ones and a multitude from the later ones." Someone else analysed it: the meaning is "they are a multitude from the earlier ones," i.e. a group of those who came before the mission of the Prophet ﷺ and a group of the followers of the Prophet ﷺ. The holder of this view said: In the first [passage] it was said "a multitude from the earlier ones and a few from the later ones," and in the second "a multitude from the earlier ones and a multitude from the later ones," only because the first is about those who were foremost in following the prophets ﷺ, and those who were foremost in following them before the Prophet ﷺ are more numerous than those who were foremost in following the Prophet ﷺ. What shows you the soundness of this is that the people of Yūnus ﷺ believed, and they were a hundred thousand or more, and the sorcerers followed Mūsā ﷺ, and they are related to have been more than these; for this reason it was said "and a few from the later ones." The second multitude is for the Companions of the Right, not for the forerunners, and the Companions of the Right may include the Muslims until the Day of Resurrection. This is according to this view, and we have mentioned another. And Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows best.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: وَأَصْحابُ الشِّمالِ: i.e. those who were given their books in their left hands. It was also said: those who are taken towards the left. Qatāda said: ما أَصْحابُ الشِّمالِ, i.e. what is there for them and what has been prepared for them!

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: i.e. in the heat (ḥasr) of the Fire [Translator's note: so in the printed text, «حسر»; possibly for «حرّ», "heat"] and what reaches [one] of its flame. Ibn al-Sikkīt reported سمام as a plural of سموم. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is by dropping the augment, which is the wāw. «وحميم»: it is the hot water with which they are punished, which they are made to gulp and which is poured on their heads, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: يَطُوفُونَ بَيْنَها وَبَيْنَ حَمِيمٍ آنٍ [al-Raḥmān: 44].

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: [يحموم] is fully declined whether definite or indefinite, because there is no yafʿūl among the verb patterns.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t:
لا بارِدٍ: i.e. it has no shade that shelters. وَلا كَرِيمٍ: because it is painful. You put لا بارِدٍ in the genitive as a naʿt (adjective), and «لا» does not separate the naʿt from the qualified noun because of its wide range of use. وَلا كَرِيمٍ is conjoined to it. The grammarians permitted the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), as [the poet] said: [kāmil metre] 457-
وتريك وجها كالصّحيفة لا ... ظمآن مختلج ولا جهم
(She shows you a face like a page [smooth and fair], neither gaunt and twitching nor sullen.)

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: i.e. in the world. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he says: living in luxury.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: وَكانُوا يُصِرُّونَ: Ibn Zayd said: they do not repent and do not seek forgiveness. Persistence (al-iṣrār) in the language is remaining upon a thing and not desisting from it. عَلَى الْحِنْثِ الْعَظِيمِ: al-Farrāʾ said: He is saying: idolatry (al-shirk) is the great sin.

nahhas-irab:47-47.t:
وَكانُوا يَقُولُونَ أَإِذا مِتْنا وَكُنَّا تُراباً وَعِظاماً أَإِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ: They wondered at this; that is why the interrogative came. Abū Jaʿfar said: whoever says إذا متنا [i.e. أئذا with lightened hamza] brings the second hamza "between-between" (bayna bayna), so it is vowelled as it was before the lightening; this is what Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā Thaʿlab said: a between-between hamza is neither vowelled nor vowelless. Abū Jaʿfar said: As for writing it, it is with alif only, because it is initial and then the alif of the interrogative entered on it.

إذا is in the position of the accusative as an adverb (ẓarf). It is not permissible for لمبعوثون to govern it, because it is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ» and so cannot govern what precedes it; what governs it is متنا. One says مُتنا according to the dialect of those who say مات يموت, and it is the eloquent one; and whoever says مِتنا follows the dialect of those who say مات يمات, like خاف يخاف. It was also said: it is on [the pattern] faʿila yafʿulu, which came anomalously. [Translator's note: the vowelling distinguishing مُتنا and مِتنا has been lost in the printed text and is supplied here from the explanation.]

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: Conjoined to the position [of the noun of إنّ], and it may be conjoined to the nominative latent pronoun.

nahhas-irab:49-50.t:
Sībawayh reported, as heard from the Arabs: ادخلوا الأول فالأول ("Enter, the first, then the first [i.e. one after another]"), and claimed that it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) although it has the alif and lām. Ibn Kaysān said: We know of nothing that is sound in the speech of the Arabs in the accusative as a ḥāl and having the alif and lām except this. The reason for it is that it occurred to distinguish between two meanings: if you say دخلوا أولا أولا, its meaning is "they entered separately," and if you say دخلوا الأول فالأول, its meaning is "I know them [as] the first, then the first." Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: the definiteness only came afterwards, so the alif and lām were brought as redundant (zāʾida), like other augments. Sībawayh reported from ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar: أدخلوا الأولَ فالأولَ ("make them enter, the first then the first"), construing it according to the meaning, and Sībawayh judged him wrong, because ادخلوا الأول فالأول فالأول is not permissible, i.e. it is only said with the lām [Translator's note: the passage is obscure in the printed text and is translated as written]. Someone else argued for ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar that it is construed according to the meaning, just as it is related from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that he read فبذلك فلتفرحوا [Yūnus: 58].

[On أوّل:] A verb ought to be pronounced from أوّل, since it is equivalent to الأفضل [i.e. an elative, which normally has a verb], but that is rejected because its fāʾ and ʿayn [first and second radicals] are from one place [i.e. the same letter], and no verb like this is found in the speech of the Arabs, while among nouns it is rare. They said كوكب for the bulk of a thing; they said for amusement and play ددا, ددن and دد; and they said for a blunt sword ددان — nothing other than these is known with dāl. In the ḥadīth from ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him: "until the people become ببّان واحد," i.e. one single thing; and «بيّة» is a nickname. Nothing other than these two is known in the speech of the Arabs with bāʾ. As for their saying ببّغاء for the bird [the parrot] and ببر for a beast of prey, they are both foreign. This is hardly known in letters other than these, except a little if it occurs; they said آء for a kind of plant, and no parallel to it is known. For this reason no verb was used from أوّل.

Sībawayh reported that «أول» may be fully declined as being a noun, not an adjective, as one says ما ترك أولا ولا آخرا ("he left neither first nor last"), and its not being fully declined was reported, as being an adjective.

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ أَيُّهَا الضَّالُّونَ: i.e. those who deviate from the path of guidance. الْمُكَذِّبُونَ: [denying] the threat and the resurrection.

nahhas-irab:52-53.t:
لَآكِلُونَ مِنْ شَجَرٍ مِنْ زَقُّومٍ فَمالِؤُنَ مِنْهَا: [مِنها is] according to treating the group as feminine; had it been منه, treating the whole as masculine, it would have been permissible. الْبُطُونَ is the plural of بطن, which is masculine. As for the poet's saying: [ṭawīl metre] 458-
فإنّ كلابا هذه عشر أبطن ... وأنت بريء من قبائلها العشر
(For Kilāb — these are ten clans [lit. "bellies"], and you are free of its ten tribes.)
it is feminine because of the femininity of "tribe," construed according to the meaning; had it been masculine according to the wording, it would have been permissible.

nahhas-irab:54-54.t: عَلَيْهِ: on the trees, treating the whole as masculine; and it may refer to the eating [i.e. to الأكل].

nahhas-irab:55-55.t:
This is the reading of most of the readers. Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī read فَشارِبُونَ شُرْبَ الْهِيمِ with fatḥa on the shīn [i.e. شَرب]. Abū ʿUbayd claimed that it is the dialect of the Prophet ﷺ — an appalling statement. Some of the scholars said: his saying "the dialect of the Prophet ﷺ" is an appalling statement which no one should say except with certainty; and the ḥadīth which the ḥadīth scholars and its transmitters relate from the Prophet ﷺ, in which they say «إنّها أيام أكل وشرب» ("they are days of eating and drinking") with ḍamma on the shīn, is other than this — or [only] those of them who said so. A parallel to this is his saying "the dialect of the Prophet ﷺ" about «الحرب خدعة» ("war is deception"), whereas both خدعة and خدعة [i.e. khadʿa and khudʿa] have been heard.

The position on this, according to the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, is that شَربا with fatḥa on the shīn is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and شُربا with ḍamma is a noun for the maṣdar, more often used here; and شَرب is used as the plural of شارب (drinker), as [the poet] said: [basīṭ metre] 459-
فقلت للشّرب في درنا وقد ثملوا ... شيموا وكيف يشيم الشّارب الثّمل
(I said to the drinking company in Durnā, when they were drunk: "Watch [for the lightning]!" — but how can a drunken drinker watch?)
«والهيم» is the plural of هيماء and أهيم; it is on [the pattern] fuʿl, and the hāʾ was given kasra because if it were given ḍamma the yāʾ would turn into wāw. al-Farrāʾ permitted الهيم to be the plural of هائم.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: هذا نُزُلُهُمْ: i.e. that with which Allah will host them on the Day of Resurrection, and it is the Day of Judgement, on which He will recompense people for their deeds.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t: i.e. We created you when you were nothing, and brought you into being as human beings; so why do you not believe that the One who did that will give you life and resurrect you?

nahhas-irab:58-58.t:
أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ: i.e. O you who deny the resurrection and reject the power of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, to bring them to life.
ما تُمْنُونَ: into the wombs of women. al-Farrāʾ said: one says أمنى and منى, and أمنى is more common.

nahhas-irab:59-59.t: أَأَنْتُمْ تَخْلُقُونَهُ: i.e. is it you who create that sperm until the spirit comes into it, أَمْ نَحْنُ الْخالِقُونَ?

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: نَحْنُ قَدَّرْنا بَيْنَكُمُ الْمَوْتَ: i.e. so among you are those whose term is near and those whose term is far, all of that by decree. وَما نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ: i.e. regarding your terms, and nothing is done in them over Our heads; rather they are as We have decreed.

nahhas-irab:61-61.t: عَلى أَنْ نُبَدِّلَ أَمْثالَكُمْ: The best of what has been said about its meaning: We have decreed death among you on [the basis] that We replace your likes, i.e. We bring others than you of your kind. وَنُنْشِئَكُمْ فِي ما لا تَعْلَمُونَ: The best of what has been said about its meaning: and We bring you into being in forms other than these; so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, will bring the believers into being on the Day of Resurrection in the best of forms even if they were ugly in the world, and will bring the unbelievers and the sinners into being in the ugliest of forms even if they were noble [in appearance] in the world.

nahhas-irab:62-62.t: وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ النَّشْأَةَ الْأُولى فَلَوْلا تَذَكَّرُونَ: i.e. you know that We brought you into being when you did not exist; so why do you not take heed and know that the One who did that is able to bring you to life? The origin is تتذكّرون; the tāʾ was assimilated into the dhāl.

nahhas-irab:63-63.t: ما may be a maṣdar [particle], i.e. "your tilling," and it may have the meaning of الذي (relative noun), i.e. "Have you considered the tilth which you till?"

nahhas-irab:64-64.t: The meaning of تزرعونه is "you make it a crop"; for this reason the ḥadīth came from Abū Hurayra from the Prophet ﷺ; he said: "Do not say 'I grew [crops] (zaraʿtu)'; rather say 'I tilled (ḥarathtu).'" Then Abū Hurayra recited: أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ ما تَحْرُثُونَ أَأَنْتُمْ تَزْرَعُونَهُ أَمْ نَحْنُ الزَّارِعُونَ.

nahhas-irab:65-66.t:
لَوْ نَشاءُ لَجَعَلْناهُ حُطاماً: i.e. crushed, of no benefit. فَظَلْتُمْ تَفَكَّهُونَ: The scholars differed about its meaning. al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said: تفكّهون, i.e. you regret the acts of disobedience you committed in the past, for which you were punished with this. ʿIkrima said: تفكّهون means you blame one another, i.e. for the obedience to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, that you missed. It was also said: تفكّهون means you enjoy yourselves; on this view the implied construction is "Have you considered what you till, so that you went on enjoying yourselves with it?" Abū Jaʿfar said: The most appropriate of the views is what Mujāhid said; he said: تفكّهون means you wonder, i.e. some of you make others wonder at what has befallen them. Its origin is from تفكّه القوم بالحديث, when people make one another wonder at it.

It is related that it is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]: فَظَلْتُمْ with kasra on the ẓāʾ [i.e. فظِلتم]. The origin is ظللتم, as [the poet] said: [ṭawīl metre] 460-
ظللت بها أبكي وأبكي إلى الغد
(I remained there weeping, and weeping until the morrow.)
Whoever says ظَلتم dropped the lām that had kasra, for lightness; and whoever says ظِلتم cast the vowel of the lām onto the ẓāʾ after dropping it. [The origin of تفكّهون] is تتفكّهون. The meaning is: you say إِنَّا لَمُغْرَمُونَ. ʿIkrima said: "we are being pursued [by misfortune]." Qatāda said: "we are being punished." It was also said: "we have suffered loss in our crops." The view of Qatāda is good and clear, because it is known in the speech of the Arabs that punishment and destruction are called غرام. al-Aʿshā said: [khafīf metre] 461-
إن يعاقب يكن غراما وإن يعط ... جزيلا فإنّه لا يبالي
(If he punishes, it is a lasting torment; and if he gives abundantly, he does not care [how much].)

nahhas-irab:67-67.t: i.e. we are not those suffering loss; rather we have been deprived and denied our livelihood.

nahhas-irab:68-68.t: الَّذِي is in the position of the accusative, and تَشْرَبُونَ is its ṣila (relative clause); the implied form is تشربونه — the hāʾ was dropped because of the length of the noun, and that is good because it is the end of a verse.

nahhas-irab:69-69.t: أَأَنْتُمْ أَنْزَلْتُمُوهُ مِنَ الْمُزْنِ: The origin is أأنتم; the second hamza was lightened and pronounced "between-between" (bayna bayna). The evidence that it is vowelled while being between-between is that the nūn after it is vowelless. The preference of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh is to pronounce it between-between because of the heaviness of two hamzas coming together. أَمْ نَحْنُ الْمُنْزِلُونَ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:70-70.t: لَوْ نَشاءُ جَعَلْناهُ أُجاجاً: al-Farrāʾ said: الأجاج is salty water of intense bitterness. فَلَوْلا تَشْكُرُونَ: i.e. why do you not thank the One who did not make it salty, so that you could not benefit from it for drinking or crops?

nahhas-irab:71-71.t: One of the scholars said: i.e. which you see with your eyes. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is an error; had it been as he said, it would have been ترون. It is only from أوريت الزند أوريه, when you strike the fire-stick [to kindle fire].

nahhas-irab:72-72.t:
أَأَنْتُمْ أَنْشَأْتُمْ شَجَرَتَها: i.e. did you invent it and bring it into being? أَمْ نَحْنُ الْمُنْشِؤُنَ: If you wish, you may pronounce the hamza between-between, i.e. between hamza and wāw. For this reason Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: it may only be written with wāw, i.e. with two wāws, and likewise «يستهزئون»; whoever writes it with yāʾ has erred in his view, because the ḍamma is the strongest of the vowels, so when the hamza has ḍamma and is in the middle [of the word], what precedes it has no bearing. Whoever substitutes [a letter] for the hamza says المنشوون and المستهزوون. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a poor, anomalous dialect, found only in a little poetry.

I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān relate that the correct [report] of Sībawayh's view is that he does not permit substituting [another letter for] the hamza — meaning outside poetry. He said: because Abū Zayd said to him: "Some of the Arabs say قرا without a hamza." Sībawayh said to him: "Then how do they say it in the imperfect?" He said: "يقرا." He said: "Then this is wrong, because they ought to say يقري, so that it would be like رمى يرمي." Abū al-Ḥasan said: So this from Sībawayh indicates that he does not permit it.

nahhas-irab:73-73.t:
نَحْنُ جَعَلْناها تَذْكِرَةً: two objects; i.e. something that serves as a reminder. وَمَتاعاً لِلْمُقْوِينَ: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: المقوون are the travellers. Ibn Zayd said: المقوي is the hungry one. Abū Jaʿfar said: The origin of this is from أقوت الدّار, i.e. the abode became empty, as ʿAntara said: [kāmil metre] 462-
حييت من طلل تقادم عهده ... أقوى وأقفر بعد أمّ الهيثم
(Be greeted, O ruin whose time has grown old, which has become empty and desolate after Umm al-Haytham.)
One says أقوى when someone alights in القيّ, i.e. empty land; and أقوى when his companions are strong, i.e. free of weakness.

nahhas-irab:74-74.t: i.e. by mentioning Him and His most beautiful names.

nahhas-irab:75-80.t:
تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ (80)
فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِمَواقِعِ النُّجُومِ: The view of Ibn ʿAbbās is that it is the descent [in instalments] of the Qur'an, and al-Farrāʾ adduced as proof of the soundness of that the fact that after it comes وَإِنَّهُ لَقَسَمٌ لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ (76). The view of al-Ḥasan: i.e. by the places where the stars set. Muḥammad ibn Jarīr claimed that this view is more likely to be correct, because what is commonly understood by النجوم is that they are the rising [stars]. إِنَّهُ لَقُرْآنٌ كَرِيمٌ (77) فِي كِتابٍ مَكْنُونٍ (78): i.e. protected. لا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ (79): [part] of the naʿt (adjective) of the Book. تَنْزِيلٌ: [part] of the naʿt of the Qur'an, i.e. possessing descent (dhū tanzīl), i.e. sent down مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ.

nahhas-irab:81-81.t: i.e. you soften your speech towards whoever disbelieves in this protected Book.

nahhas-irab:82-82.t:
It is related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read وتجعلون شكركم أنكم تكذّبون ("and you make your thanks that you deny"), and from Ibn ʿAbbās: وتجعلون شكركم أنكم تكذّبون. Abū Jaʿfar said:
These two readings are by way of explanation, and it is not to be interpreted of any of the Companions that he read contrary to what is in the agreed-upon Muṣḥaf; and likewise the tafsīr. The meaning according to the reading of the multitude is "and you make the thanks for your provision," then [the muḍāf] was omitted, like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [Yūsuf: 82]. Ibn ʿAbbās explained how this denial came from them; he said: they say "we were given rain by such-and-such a star (nawʾ)," and the Prophet ﷺ called this unbelief. Abū Isḥāq said: Its parallel is the astrologer's saying: "When such-and-such a star rises and a person then travels, such-and-such will happen." So this is denial of Allah's warning, Majestic and Mighty.

nahhas-irab:84-84.t:
An address to whoever is present with a dying person. The implied construction is: "then why do you not bring it back, if you are truthful?" One says رجع and رجعته [i.e. the verb is both intransitive and transitive]; on this basis He said تَرْجِعُونَها إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ (87) — [truthful] in [claiming] that you are not owned and governed.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is how al-Farrāʾ reported the meaning of مَدِينِينَ; he said: owned. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: غَيْرَ مَدِينِينَ, i.e. not to be called to account. al-Ḥasan said: not to be resurrected. It was also said: not to be recompensed, from His saying, Mighty and Majestic: مالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ [al-Fātiḥa: 4]. As for the apodosis (jawāb) of the second لولا, there are two views on it. al-Farrāʾ said: both were answered with a single apodosis. It was also said: it was omitted from one of them, and the other indicates it.

nahhas-irab:89-89.t:
فَأَمَّا إِنْ كانَ مِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ: i.e. as for [the case that] the deceased is among those brought near to the mercy of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, he will have rest and fragrance. Abū Jaʿfar said: This place is difficult in i'rab, because «أما» requires an apodosis (jawāb), and it is asked why only a noun follows «أما», while it resembles the conditional particles, and it is a verb that follows the conditional particles. This is the most difficult thing about it.

As for the apodosis of «أما» and «إن», there is disagreement about it among the grammarians. The view of al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ is that both were answered with a single apodosis, which is the fāʾ and what follows it. As for the view of Sībawayh, «إن» has no apodosis here, because after it comes a past verb, as you say: أنا أكرمتك إن جئتني ("I honoured you, if you came to me"). The view of Muḥammad ibn Yazīd is that the apodosis of «إن» is omitted, because what comes after it indicates it.

Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Abū Isḥāq being asked about the meaning of «أما». He said: it is for moving from one thing to another, i.e. leave what we were on and take up something else. As for the discussion of the reason why only a noun follows it: Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān mentioned that the meaning of «أما» is "whatever may be the case" (مهما يكن من شيء), so أما was made to stand for the verb, and a verb does not follow a verb, so it was necessary for a noun to follow it. Its implied position is after its apodosis. So if you want [to know] the i'rab of the noun that follows it, put «مهما» in its place and imagine the noun after the fāʾ. You say أما زيدا فضربت, its meaning being "whatever may be the case, I struck Zayd."

Budayl ibn Maysara related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaqīq from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Prophet ﷺ read فَرَوْحٌ with ḍamma on the rāʾ [i.e. فرُوح], and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read likewise. Abū Jaʿfar said: The isnad (chain of transmission) of this ḥadīth is fair; some of them say in it: from Budayl from Abū al-Jawzāʾ from ʿĀʾisha from the Prophet ﷺ. The meaning of the ḍamma is "everlasting life." Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās on فَرَوْحٌ وَرَيْحانٌ; he said: a place of rest. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: الرّوح is joy. Hushaym related from Juwaybir from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: فروح; he said: rest. Someone else related from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: فروح; he said: forgiveness and mercy. He said: الروح among the people of language is joy, as Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said, and forgiveness and mercy are a source of joy.

As for وريحان, there are three views on its meaning. Among them: it is provision. Among them: it is rest. Among them: it is the fragrant herb (rayḥān) that is smelled; this is the view of al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, Abū al-ʿĀliya and Abū al-Jawzāʾ, and it is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar; he said: when the departure of the believer's soul draws near, the angel brings him rayḥān; he smells it and his soul departs. Abū Isḥāq said: the origin of ريحان is ريّحان [Translator's note: the doubling is not shown in the printed text, which has «ريحان ريحان»], the first yāʾ being changed from a wāw; its origin is روحان: the wāw was assimilated into the yāʾ, then it was lightened, as one says ميت; except that it is not used in the original form except far-fetchedly, because it has an augmented alif and nūn. وَجَنَّةُ نَعِيمٍ: i.e. and he will have, along with that, a garden of bliss.

nahhas-irab:90-90.t: i.e. among those who are taken towards the right, to the Garden.

nahhas-irab:91-91.t: There are [several] views on it. Qatāda said: فَسَلامٌ لَكَ مِنْ أَصْحابِ الْيَمِينِ: they are safe from the punishment of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and the angels greeted them. It was also said: فَسَلامٌ لَكَ مِنْ أَصْحابِ الْيَمِينِ (91), i.e. for you there is a greeting from them, i.e. they greet you. This view is open to examination, because the address is to the Prophet ﷺ, so it is not to be shifted to someone else except with decisive evidence. It was also said: فَسَلامٌ لَكَ: it is granted to you that you are among the Companions of the Right, «أنّ» having been omitted, the meaning being "because you are among the Companions of the Right." Omitting «أنّ» is an error in Arabic, because what comes after it is included in its ṣila (relative clause), even though the one who held this view is al-Farrāʾ, and Muḥammad ibn Jarīr adopted it.

nahhas-irab:92-92.t: i.e. those who deviate from the path.

nahhas-irab:93-93.t: فَنُزُلٌ: i.e. a punishment مِنْ حَمِيمٍ, which is the boiling water.

nahhas-irab:95-95.t: The Kufans permit annexing a thing to itself and count this among it. In the view of the Basrans that is an error, because a thing is explained by something other than itself, and the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) is what [the muḍāf] is explained by. Mujāhid said: حقّ اليقين means "the truth of the certain report." Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is that this which We have narrated in this sūra is certainty, the truth of certainty, as you say "so-and-so is a scholar, the true scholar" when you go to great lengths in emphasis.

nahhas-irab:96-96.t: i.e. so declare Allah, Majestic and Mighty, transcendent above their unbelief, by His most beautiful names.
